RESULT
precipitate of pure and dry BaS04 is obtained by treating BaC12 solution with H2S04 solution followed by washing and drying.
PRECAUTIONS
1. The precipitation should be complete.
2. During washing by decantation, there should not be any loss of the
precipitate.
3. All the glasswares should be handled with care.
4. While drying the ppt over burner, care should be taken so that the
filter paper does not burn.
5. The precipitant should never be added in a very large excess.
Note: The ppt can be obtained in the crystalline state. In order to coagulate the ppt, boiling is done.
SUGGESTED WORKS
To obtain the precipitate of calcium carbonate in pure and dry state I. by treating calcium chloride solution with sodium carbonate solution.
To obtain the pure and dry barium sulphite solid by treating sodium sulphite solution with barium chloride solution.
To obtain the pure and dry lead chloride solid by treating lead nitrate solution with dilute hydrochloric acid.

EXPERIMENT NO. 6
Object: TO PREPARE FAIRLY PURE WATER FROM THE IMPURE
WATER BY DISTILLATION METHOD
APPARATUS REQUIRED
Beaker
1. Distillation flask or glass retort with lid
Test tubes
3. Conical flask (receiver)
Stand and clamp
5. Watch glass
7. Condenser or water trough
CHEMICALS REQUIRED
1. Silver nitrate solution
2. Barium chloride solution
3. Litmus papers
THEORY

Pure water can be obtained from its impure sample by distillation method. The conversion of a liquid substance into its vapour by heating followed by conversion of the vapour into the liquid form by cooling is called distillation. In other words, distillation is defined as the process of evaporation by the application of heat followed by cooling. The pure liquid obtained in the receiver after condensation is called distillate.

After the above tests are performed, half fill the glass retort with the impure water, close it and fit the apparatus as shown in figure.
Heat the retort first gently and then strongly so as to keep the liquid boiling.
The conical flask is kept under water in a trough. Put wet filter paper on the outer wall of the conical flask.
The steam which is obtained under the action of heat passes through the long neck of the retort. The steam condenses in the receiver where pure water is collected as 'distillate'.
